rule: M-107 - registered BEFORE any statistic was computed for these tests. The recorded_utc above precedes the first execution of tools/prereg_outside_tests.py. Anyone can verify by comparing this file's commit time to the commit time of the results artifact.
purpose: Two OUTSIDE tests requested explicitly as falsification gates. Both are written to KILL, not to confirm. Nothing in this programme has survived a correctly-specified kill test yet, so the prior is that these die too; a survival would be the first evidence worth acting on.

tests.question: Does the daily-breakout gross edge concentrate in HIGH realised-volatility regimes strongly enough to clear a 24 bp round-trip cost?

specification.rule: Donchian lookback 20 on the prior 20 bars; signal = close above prior high; entry at NEXT bar open; TP = entry + 2.0 x ATR(14); SL = entry - 1.0 x ATR(14); max hold 10 bars then exit at that bar close; one position at a time; stop checked before target within a bar (pessimistic).
specification.volatility_bucket: realised volatility of DAILY RETURNS measured over the 20 bars ENDING AT THE SIGNAL BAR (t-1), i.e. known before the fill. Terciles formed PER MARKET over that market's whole trade sample, so each market contributes its own low/mid/high bucket. Pooling across markets after per-market bucketing.
specification.data: daily bars, full available history per market
specification.split_basis_named: calendar (per-market terciles on realised vol, then pooled)

KILL_CONDITION.statement: KILL the family if EITHER holds: (i) the TOP realised-vol tercile net edge < 0 bp after 24 bp round trip, OR (ii) the TOP tercile gross edge < 24 bp.
KILL_CONDITION.test_stat: mean net edge per trade in the top realised-vol tercile, and mean gross edge in the same tercile

tests.note: This is the most favourable framing of the breakout family that exists in this programme: it selects the regime where the edge should be largest and charges a cost (24bp) that is BELOW the 10bp/side conservative case. If it dies here it dies everywhere.

tests.question: Does the crypto lead survive an out-of-sample deflated Sharpe test against the full 67-cell search it was selected from, and does it realise a usable edge in forward trading?

specification.dsr_method: Bailey & Lopez de Prado deflated Sharpe: P(true SR > 0) given n_trials=67, using skew and kurtosis of the return series.
specification.observations: rows from reports/forward_observations.jsonl tagged H-119, WITH PROVENANCE TRACKED: rows whose created_at precedes their closed_at are genuine forward observations; rows created after their close are backfilled and are reported separately and NEVER counted as forward.

KILL_CONDITION.statement: KILL the crypto lead if EITHER holds: (i) DSR p >= 0.5 after 200 forward prints, OR (ii) any single 50-trade window realises < 10 bp net per trade.

tests.EVALUABILITY: NOT YET EVALUABLE. This test requires 200 GENUINE FORWARD prints. As of registration the forward count is 0 (all 430 H-119 ledger rows were established as a 2026-11-19 backfill in the R8 audit). The test is registered now so that it cannot be retro-fitted after the forward record accumulates. Component (ii) CAN be evaluated on historical rows and is reported as a historical diagnostic, explicitly labelled as such.
